data.title: Review native console music bundles and playback
data.description: Review bn-19q at commit bee8724. Focus on .cmusic parser correctness and validation, [audio].bundle build conflicts/provenance, native .cmusic/cart/project playback dispatch and authored-loop sample cursor semantics, compatibility of ABC/MIDI flags and exit codes, documentation accuracy, and regression coverage. Full just check and skill validators pass.

data.body: HIGH: Authored native loops stop using the native runtime after the first pass. run_native_play hard-codes RenderOpts { loops: 1 } and then SampleCursor jumps back to the cached PCM offset at intro_frames. That is not equivalent to another sequencer pass because echo feedback/delay state, the master tone filter, hiss/noise state, and channel oscillator/modulation phase persist across pattern boundaries. I confirmed this with the checked-in examples/native-music track: a real two-pass render reports intro 32 + 2 x loop 32, but its first and second loop PCM hashes differ (d4b7089e... versus 9d30ce59...); this playback path will repeat the first hash forever. That contradicts the documented claim that native synth/effect behavior matches the game and authored loops repeat naturally. Please keep the Console/sequencer rendering across host playback (or otherwise prove a state-equivalent loop boundary) and add a regression that compares playback's second pass with an actual core-rendered second pass.

MEDIUM: Native one-shots do not render the core's release ramp before playback ends or --repeat wraps. render_song returns immediately after the last pattern frame; stop_music() only arms Channel::stop() during the post-render sequencer advance, and this path sends no following frame through Audio::render. The non-repeating cursor therefore drops from the last sample straight to host zero, while --repeat jumps straight to sample 0. I reproduced this with carts/ribbit-recoil.cart song 16: the final 64 PCM samples of the exact native render are all nonzero (the last sample is 10084 in 16-bit PCM), so both modes create a hard edge. The ABC/MIDI path explicitly renders a silent release frame for this reason. Please drain/render the native click-guard release for one-shots and cover the tail/repeat seam in tests.

data.reason: Native playback is not runtime-equivalent for authored loops: it repeats cached first-pass PCM even when the core's stateful synth/effects produce a different next pass. Native one-shots also skip the armed release ramp and hard-cut/wrap.

data.body: Addressed in 18b1eb8. Native device playback now owns one stateful Console on a renderer thread and feeds a bounded frame queue, so authored passes are never replayed from cached PCM. A regression compares two streamed passes byte-for-byte with music render loops=2 and proves the two real loop PCM spans differ. Natural one-shots now drain the core release frame before stop/restart; explicit --seconds cuts fade their last 64 samples. Added one-shot/repeat/clip seam tests, updated docs, passed strict clippy, focused CLI tests, a real zero-volume host-device smoke, both skill validators, and full just check.

Re-review at exact HEAD b3301b3: the continuous NativeFrameRenderer path now matches two real core loop passes, and the queue's normal stop/error/deadline cleanup is coherent. Two actionable issues remain. HIGH: run_native_play still calls render_song and discards its complete Vec before starting the bounded renderer (preview.rs:604-611). Thus device playback still caches an entire pass up front despite the new two-second-queue contract. A tiny valid cart can chain 64 patterns whose shared 32-row speed=255 SFX makes one pass 522,240 frames / about 1.54 GiB of f32 PCM, and --seconds accepts finite values that cast up to u64::MAX; either can OOM/hang before the queue exists. Compute the report from the already-built SongPlan/clip bound or stream validation without retaining PCM, and add a large-bound regression. MEDIUM: the one-shot regression has no echo section and proves silence only for dry voices. One release frame drains the 64-sample channel click guard, but the native echo bus persists longer; playback still cuts or restarts after that single frame. I reproduced an allowed high-feedback one-shot whose release frame ended at -1135 in 16-bit PCM (last-64 peak 1885), leaving a hard seam. Drain/fade the effect tail to a silent boundary and cover an echo-enabled one-shot/repeat.

data.reason: At b3301b3, authored loops are stateful, but non-dry-run still pre-renders and retains an unbounded full pass before the bounded queue, permitting small valid inputs or huge --seconds values to OOM/hang. Echo-enabled one-shots also remain non-silent at the one-frame release seam.

data.body: Re-reviewed exact HEAD e6813b91e7282766d821b728e6ce6380a98a3b63. The remaining HIGH is fixed: run_native_play now calls plan_song directly, derives reporting and finite playback deadlines from SongPlan or the explicit frame bound, and no longer calls render_song or allocates/discards full PCM before native streaming. An extreme --seconds 1e300 --volume 0 device smoke streamed until the 10s timeout without OOM or panic. The remaining MEDIUM is fixed: the one-shot release frame is tail-faded to an exactly silent final sample, and the regression now uses high-feedback echo, proves the wet tail remains nonzero beyond the dry/core release region, and asserts the final sample and repeat seam are zero. Independent verification passed: cargo test -p console --lib music::preview::tests (14), cargo test -p console --test music_native (3), cargo clippy -p console --all-targets -- -D warnings, both build-cart skill validators, git diff --check, and full just check including workspace tests/doctests and web smoke. No remaining actionable findings.
